I have everything I need.

## What this is

**eShop** — the Microsoft reference **e-commerce microservices sample built on .NET Aspire**. It is an application (not a library): 19 projects in `eShop.slnx:1-29`, split into ASP.NET Core services, two MAUI clients, and shared infrastructure libraries. The composition root is `src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj:1`, which uses `Sdk="Aspire.AppHost.Sdk/13.2.0"` and `<OutputType>Exe</OutputType>` — this is the project you run.

## What composes the processes

`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs` is the entire topology as code. It builds a `DistributedApplication` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:3`) and calls `builder.Build().Run()` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:103`). Aspire launches each `AddProject<...>` as a separate OS process and each container resource via Docker/Podman.

**Backing infrastructure containers** (started first, projects `WaitFor` them):
- Redis `"redis"` — `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:7`
- RabbitMQ `"eventbus"`, persistent lifetime — `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:8-9`
- Postgres `"postgres"` on the `ankane/pgvector` image — `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:10-13`, carving out four databases `catalogdb`, `identitydb`, `orderingdb`, `webhooksdb` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:15-18`)

**The 9 .NET processes that start:**

| Process (Aspire name) | Kind | Declared at | Host code |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity-api` | IdentityServer + MVC, external endpoint | `Program.cs:23-26` | `src/Identity.API/Program.cs:18-37` (`AddIdentityServer`, `MapDefaultControllerRoute` at :55) |
| `basket-api` | **gRPC only** — no HTTP API | `Program.cs:30-33` | `src/Basket.API/Program.cs:6,12` (`AddGrpc`, `MapGrpcService<BasketService>`) |
| `catalog-api` | Minimal-API Web API, versioned | `Program.cs:36-38` | `src/Catalog.API/Program.cs:21` (`MapCatalogApi`) |
| `ordering-api` | Minimal-API Web API, versioned + authorized | `Program.cs:40-44` | `src/Ordering.API/Program.cs:19-22` (`MapOrdersApiV1().RequireAuthorization()`) |
| `order-processor` | **Worker** (no HTTP surface) | `Program.cs:46-49` | `src/OrderProcessor/Program.cs:1-10`; runs `GracePeriodManagerService : BackgroundService` (`src/OrderProcessor/Services/GracePeriodManagerService.cs:12`, registered `src/OrderProcessor/Extensions/Extensions.cs:18`) |
| `payment-processor` | **Worker** — pure bus subscriber | `Program.cs:51-52` | `src/PaymentProcessor/Program.cs:5-6` subscribes only to `OrderStatusChangedToStockConfirmedIntegrationEvent` |
| `webhooks-api` | Minimal-API Web API | `Program.cs:54-57` | `src/Webhooks.API/Program.cs:20-21` |
| `webhooksclient` | Blazor Server UI | `Program.cs:65-67` | `src/WebhookClient/Program.cs:5` (`AddRazorComponents().AddInteractiveServerComponents()`) |
| `webapp` | Blazor Server storefront, external endpoint | `Program.cs:69-77` | `src/WebApp/Program.cs:8,30` |

Plus one non-project process: **`mobile-bff`**, a YARP reverse proxy fronting catalog/ordering/identity for mobile clients — `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:60-62`, routes defined in `src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:185-249`.

**Not started by the AppHost:** `ClientApp` and `HybridApp` are .NET MAUI apps (`src/ClientApp/ClientApp.csproj:4,18`, `src/HybridApp/HybridApp.csproj:4,18`) — they are in the solution and deployed to devices/emulators separately. `eShop.ServiceDefaults`, `EventBus`, `EventBusRabbitMQ`, `IntegrationEventLogEF`, `Ordering.Domain`, `Ordering.Infrastructure`, `WebAppComponents` are class libraries, and the 5 `tests/` projects don't run either.

## Runnable entry points inside those processes

110 entry points total, across six kinds:

- **43 HTTP endpoints** — Catalog (`/api/catalog/items`, `.../withsemanticrelevance/{text}`, etc.) and Ordering (`POST /api/orders/`, `PUT /api/orders/cancel`, `PUT /api/orders/ship`, `POST /api/orders/draft`, `GET /api/orders/`), plus Webhooks and Identity.
- **3 gRPC methods**, all in Basket.API: `Basket.GetBasket`, `Basket.UpdateBasket`, `Basket.DeleteBasket` (`src/Basket.API/Grpc/`), backed by `RedisBasketRepository`.
- **13 RabbitMQ message consumers** — the async spine. Basket.API consumes `OrderStartedIntegrationEvent`; Catalog.API consumes `OrderStatusChangedToAwaitingValidation` and `...ToPaid`; Ordering.API consumes `GracePeriodConfirmed`, `OrderPaymentFailed`, `OrderPaymentSucceeded`, `OrderStockConfirmed`, `OrderStockRejected`; PaymentProcessor consumes `OrderStatusChangedToStockConfirmed`; WebApp consumes `OrderStatusChangedTo{Cancelled,Shipped,Submitted}`; Webhooks.API consumes `ProductPriceChanged`.
- **2 hosted services** — `GracePeriodManagerService` (OrderProcessor) and `RabbitMQEventBus` (EventBusRabbitMQ, hosted inside every subscribing process).
- **7 domain event handlers** (Ordering.API) and **42 MAUI UI entry points** (ClientApp `[RelayCommand]`s).

## The shared composition layer

Every process calls into `src/eShop.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs`. `AddServiceDefaults` (`:16`) wires service discovery (`:20`, `:28`) and standard HTTP resilience (`:25`); `AddBasicServiceDefaults` (`:40`) — used by the two non-HTTP-facing processes, Basket.API and OrderProcessor — adds health checks (`:43`) and OpenTelemetry (`:45`). All of them then call `MapDefaultEndpoints` (`:108`) to expose `/health`, which the AppHost health-checks for `identity-api` and `ordering-api` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:26,43`).

## How the processes talk

Three distinct seam styles, worth knowing before you change anything:
- **gRPC:** WebApp → Basket.API (the only Basket surface).
- **HTTP + service discovery:** WebApp → Catalog.API and Ordering.API; WebApp also proxies product images directly with `MapForwarder("/product-images/{id}", "https+http://catalog-api", ...)` (`src/WebApp/Program.cs:32`).
- **RabbitMQ publish/consume:** Ordering.API ↔ Basket.API and Catalog.API; OrderProcessor and PaymentProcessor → Ordering.API. Note that OrderProcessor and PaymentProcessor are reachable *only* over the bus.

Two wiring details that commonly surprise people: Identity.API is configured *after* the apps because it needs their callback URLs, which is a deliberate cyclic reference (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:96-101`); and `order-processor` `WaitFor(orderingApi)` not for traffic reasons but because Ordering.API owns the EF migrations for the shared `orderingdb` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:49`).

One caveat: the OpenAI and Ollama integrations are present but **off** — both `useOpenAI` and `useOllama` are hardcoded `false` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:80,86`), so the semantic-relevance catalog endpoints run without a live embedding model unless you flip those flags.
